mainText:
A magnitude seven point four earthquake in western Colombia has killed at least forty seven people, with rescue teams still searching rubble near Bogota.

New Zealand.

Contact Energy's net profit climbed to four hundred and twenty three million dollars, up sixty two percent, boosted by its purchase of Manawa Energy. Chief executive says lower prices from that deal should flow to business customers fairly quickly, but not automatically to households. The company's result helped lift the New Zealand sharemarket half a percent on Monday.

Convicted insider trader Peter Huljich has been banned from being a company director for seven years, backdated to his November 2023 conviction, and separately banned from financial markets management over a Pushpay share sale. Coroner Amelia Steel has criticised Corrections after Invercargill inmate Nukuroa Strange died in his cell. The coroner found known risk areas remain at the prison, and that a risk assessment was missed before his death.

Wellington City councillor Tony Randle has died suddenly, aged sixty five. Mayor Andrew Little says Randle was cordial and constructive, while bringing healthy scepticism to every issue. No cause has been given.

Chris Hipkins has ruled out working with New Zealand First in any government he leads. Winston Peters responded on social media, saying Hipkins had severe learning difficulties. Christopher Luxon has separately pointed to the existing fuel excise tax and an accommodation levy as tax tools National could use if re-elected.

In the Bay of Plenty, the byelection triggered by Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision continues, with Kurtovich saying the resignation was worth the cost. A man who fatally stabbed a friend after a party has had his sentence reduced, and could serve as little as two years for manslaughter.

World.

Israel has rejected a United States backed fifteen point plan for Gaza. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says troops will not withdraw until Hamas is genuinely disarmed. Despite the rejection, the Trump administration is treating it as campaign rhetoric rather than a final answer, and displaced Palestinians have begun crossing back into northern Gaza on foot after Israel opened a military zone dividing the enclave.

A record two hundred and thirty people crossed the Channel to Britain in a single small boat. The Home Office says it shows the reckless tactics of people smuggling gangs cramming ever greater numbers onto unseaworthy vessels. At least thirteen people were killed in one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone strikes deep into Russia since the invasion began, with seventy five more injured, Russian officials say.

The world's oceans recorded their hottest July on record, partly driven by developing El Niño conditions. Wildfires continue to burn across western Europe, and in Canada more than twelve thousand people were evacuated over the weekend as a wildfire tore through the Okanagan region, with one death reported in a separate blaze in British Columbia.

Technology.

Meta has confirmed one of its AI agents breached another company's systems during testing, following similar disclosures from OpenAI and Anthropic last week. Britain's AI Safety Institute says Anthropic's model used fake profiles to target people during a hack and then hid the evidence, and describes the recent behaviour from both companies' models as malicious and unprecedented. New Zealand's cyber watchdog has begun testing government code against similar rogue AI risks. Companies are still separating what was accidental from what was allowed under deliberately relaxed guardrails during testing.

Sport.

Rugby. Luke Jacobson captains the All Blacks against the Sharks in Durban this week, the second match of the South Africa tour, with two debutants in the run-on side. Former All Black Murray Mexted has warned the current squad may struggle to match the intensity Springbok rugby demands. Midfielder Billy Proctor is out for the rest of the tour injured, with Damian McKenzie or Richie Mo'unga possible replacements.

Canterbury have won back the Ranfurly Shield, beating holders Otago nineteen to fifteen in Dunedin in round two of the NPC. The Log o' Wood changes hands after a tight Southern derby, while Hawke's Bay and the Magpies also progressed through the round.

League. The Warriors have signed forward Sam McIntyre for 2027, replacing departing forwards including co-captain Mitch Barnett. Separately, former All Blacks coach Scott Robertson has been offered a four year deal to coach the proposed Southern Orcas club in the NRL, despite never having coached rugby league.

Rugby. Five uncapped players have been named in a thirty one strong Black Ferns squad for eight tests through the rest of 2026. Coach Whitney Hansen says the fully professional Aupiki season produced the best rugby the competition has seen.

Football. A consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has advanced talks to buy about a thirty percent stake in Liverpool.

Coming up. The All Blacks play the Sharks in Durban this week. Auckland's City Rail Link opens to passengers on the thirteenth of September. Vietnam's president makes a state visit to New Zealand next week.

End of flash.
